parsed.rationale: Every mismatch in the table is confined to order o2 while it occupies station p2, and all of them are the same kind of discrepancy: o2's remaining time fails to decrease on the ticks the model says it should. o2 starts on p2 at step 6 with processing time 4. Counting the ticks that follow (step 9 = tick 1, 11 = 2, 15 = 3, 18 = 4, 22 = 5, 23 = 6, 25 = 7, 26 = 8), the model decrements remaining[o2] on every tick, giving 3 at step 9, 2 at step 15, 1 at step 22 and 0 at step 25 (completion, done_at[o2] = 7, on[o2,p2] = False). The service instead reports 4, 3, 2 and 1 at those same points, and still shows o2 as processing and on p2 at step 25. The reported values drop only on ticks 2, 4, 6 and 8 — exactly every other tick. That is precisely the semantics the constant slow[st] encodes: a station flagged slow advances its processing only on every other tick. Since the service is halving o2's effective rate on p2 and no other order or station shows any anomaly, and since version 1 of the belief model hard-codes slow as false everywhere, the single revision that reconciles model and service is to set slow[p2] to true. No instance data (sku_of, qty, arrive_at, due) is implicated, because those fields were already matched at every other compared step.

explanation: revision slow[p2]=True: the recorded run (26 steps) replayed on the revised model → CORRESPONDS (all 109 compared field(s) match within the declared scope); the reference revision is slow[p2]=True (same)
